research.title: Decision tree learning
research.note: Supplies the About page facts about how Pip works: a classification tree has class labels at its leaves and feature conditions on its branches; well-known tree learners choose each question by information gain, based on entropy; and trees can become too complex and generalise poorly. The About panel also reads the article summary live when it is opened and shows the day it was read.

research.title: Overfitting
research.note: Supplies the About page fact behind the Distractions shelf: overfitting is a model fitting its data so closely that it mistakes noise for structure, and a model can improve on training data while getting worse on data it has not seen.

inspiration.title: Decision trees as a first idea of machine learning
inspiration.note: Pip is a small decision tree of at most three questions, grown by information gain with fixed tie-breaks, so training is the same every time. It is a toy that shows one idea; larger systems use many other methods and this game does not claim to show how they work.

inspiration.title: Flow Free
inspiration.note: The calm, untimed feel of a logic puzzle that is never lost.

other.title: Pyodide
other.note: Runs the game's Python learner, rules and proofs in the browser, so there is no server and no build step.

other.title: Every case, lesson and character
other.note: Pip, the workshop and all of the crates, doors, signals and other cases are invented, and the tables of cases are generated by a seeded program written for this game. None of the data is real.
